title: Module-pattern and .call(this) IIFEs: record their body declarations too
spec:
Advisory from T-15's review (.autodev/reviews/T-15.md): iifeBody recognises top-level expression-statement IIFEs only. The revealing-module pattern 'const x = (function () { ... })()' and the '(function () { ... }).call(this)' / '.bind' forms are common in older browser code and stay invisible.

ACs:
1. A top-level 'const/let/var x = (function () {...})()' (and the arrow form) has its body declarations recorded, exported:false. Check: fixture.
2. '(function () {...}).call(this)' and '.apply' / '.bind(this)()' forms likewise. Check: fixture.
3. Ordinary nested helpers stay unrecorded; the T-15 and T-12 suites stay byte-unchanged. Check: full suite.

Out of scope
- CommonJS module.exports recognition as 'exported' — deferred: who=agent:pm why=the exported-or-all fallback already yields the right steps
